transcript:
Header: 2027-02-09 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 mins | Attendees: Alex, Priya (Redwood); Mike, Sara, Jordan (NimblePayments)

Summary (auto): go over bench results, decide pinning, next steps to run perf.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:06] Mike: Mike here.
[00:08] Sara: Sara, hi.
[00:10] Jordan: Jordan present.
[00:12] Priya: Priya from Redwood.
[00:15] Alex: Cool, so agenda, short recap of last week then dive into the benchmark sheet you all ran, and model pinning decisions.
[00:25] Mike: Sounds good. we ran the nightly across our sample queries, about 5k conves — conversation snippets — and captured p95/p50 and token costs.
[00:40] Priya: I pulled the Redwood bench sheet, link in chat: https://redwood.ai/bench/nimble-poc (note: link is internal placeholder). Observations: v1.2-quant is about 30% lower latency p50 and 40% lower token cost due to quantization and kernel paths, but we saw some edge-case hallucinations on rare legal prompts. v1.1-std has slightly better factuality on those samples.
[01:05] Jordan: yeah, on the fraud-detection prompt set we saw two hallucinations where it invented a merchant name. that's a show-stopper for us if it happens in prod.
[01:15] Sara: can we mitigate with rerank or a smaller high-precision model for sensitive flows?
[01:22] Priya: absolutely — two common patterns: 1) pin to v1.2-quant for bulk routing, and 2) route sensitive flows to v1.1-std or to a guardrail/reranker. We also have fallback policies so if v1.2-quant latency spikes or quality regresses, it can auto-fallback to v1.1-std.
[01:45] Alex: Important to note, pinning is per-route. you can pin the default chat route to v1.2-quant but leave the payments/verification route pinned to v1.1-std.
[02:05] Mike: ok, that sounds reasonable. our main requirement is sub-300ms p50 for user-facing autocomplete and near-zero hallucinations on payments/legal.
[02:18] Priya: current numbers: v1.2-quant p50 ≈ 210ms, p95 ≈ 420ms on Redwood hosted in us-east; v1.1-std p50 ≈ 350ms, p95 ≈ 700ms. cost-per-1000-tokens is ~ $0.22 for v1.2-quant vs $0.65 for v1.1-std (ballpark).
[02:45] Jordan: Did you run KV cache enabled? we had caching on for prefixes but not for the short-turn prompts.
[02:52] Priya: yes we tested both; the published sheet has both cache-on and cache-off tabs. cache cuts p50 by ~15% on repeated prompts. note though, for short unique prompts the savings are smaller.
[03:18] Sara: about security— we need SOC2 type II evidence and confirm KMS/HSM integration. also SSO (SAML) for our console users.
[03:30] Alex: understood. we'll send the security pack (SOC2 report, pen test summary, KMS integration doc). Priya, can you point them to the private deployment notes for KMS?
[03:40] Priya: yeah, sending link: https://redwood.ai/security/pilot-pack (placeholder). we support customer-managed KMS for Private deploys and HSM integrations for Dedicated.
[03:55] Mike: good. also data retention — we need 90-day logs and an option for no retention for PII.
[04:05] Priya: we can set per-tenant retention, and audit log exports. We'll note that in the action items.
[04:12] Jordan: back to pinning — if we pin to v1.2-quant, what's the rollback story? let's say we detect a quality regression after a model push.
[04:21] Priya: Redwood supports canary and automatic fallback policies. suggested config: pin to v1.2-quant; enable canary rollout for 10% of traffic for any new model variant; monitor eval set metrics and automatic rollback if hallucination rate increases beyond threshold. If rollback triggers, system routes to v1.1-std.
[04:50] Alex: we should also add a shadow run for v1.1-std on sensitive flows to compare outputs without affecting users.
[05:00] Sara: good idea. Jordan, can you set up the comparison eval?
[05:05] Jordan: yep I'll do that. I'll use the bench script Priya mentioned and add our legal/fraud test cases.
[05:12] Mike: any differences in infra needs for Dedicated vs hosted during POC? we want to understand path to private.
[05:20] Priya: for the pilot we recommend hosted dedicated shared, but if you need VPC or on-prem we can do a Private deployment; that has extra setup for networking and KMS. timeline-wise Private can take 4-8 weeks depending on approvals.
[05:40] Mike: timeline is tight — we want a decision by end of next sprint (2 weeks).
[05:45] Alex: action: we'll send pricing for both hosted pinned capacity and a Dedicated reserved capacity option. estimated commit tiers included.
[05:55] Jordan: quick question: how do we handle tokenization differences across model versions? we saw slight token count diffs between v1.1 and v1.2 which affected cost.
[06:05] Priya: tokenization changed subtly between versions; recommended to normalize on the SDK layer (we provide tokenizer libs) and Redwood also reports token delta per-route so you can estimate.
[06:20] Sara: competitor question — are we comparing to Anthropic Claude and OpenAI gpt-4o in your bench?
[06:27] Priya: we included public baseline numbers, but the core comparison here is Redwood-curated open variants. we did note that gpt-4o has higher quality in some cases but cost is much higher.
[06:40] Mike: ok. So decision? draft proposal from Redwood: primary route pinned to v1.2-quant, sensitive routes pinned to v1.1-std; enable canary for new variants at 10% with auto fallback; run full perf sweep; send security docs and pricing.
[06:58] Alex: want to confirm that in chat — Jordan, you ok to run the nightly and report next Monday?
[07:04] Jordan: yes, I'll run it and upload results to the bench sheet.
[07:10] Sara: and legal will review security pack; Mike will coordinate.
[07:14] Mike: correct.
[07:16] Alex: any open blockers?
[07:18] Jordan: none from infra side.
[07:20] Mike: just need the pricing and security docs to move stakeholders.
[07:23] Alex: we'll get those over. I'll also include a recommended pinning JSON and rollout policy you can paste into the console.
[07:30] Priya: sample rollout snippet: route: /payments -> pin v1.1-std, route: /chat -> pin v1.2-quant with fallback v1.1-std, canary 10% on deploy. (note: snippet in chat)
[07:50] Alex: great. recap and next steps.
[08:00] Alex: ACTIONS: Alex send pricing & commit options; Priya share bench script + dataset; Jordan run nightly perf and upload; Mike confirm legal contact. target dates in action items.
[08:25] Sara: thanks all.
[08:28] Alex: thanks, talk next week.

Notes: some transcription artifacts: 'KV cash' instead of KV cache in one clip, 'conves' meant conversations, minor proper noun misspellings. Links and docs referenced in chat: pricing sheet (link in chat), security pack, bench sheet.
